rounds.subject: Noah
truths: He was told to bring seven pairs of every clean animal onto the ark.
He planted a vineyard after the flood and became drunk on its wine.
rounds.lie: He sent out a raven, a dove, and finally an eagle to look for dry land.
rounds.why: He sent out a raven and then a dove three times. No eagle was ever involved.

rounds.subject: Moses
truths: He was eighty years old when he first stood before Pharaoh.
He was buried by God in a valley, and no one knows his grave.
rounds.lie: He led Israel across the Jordan and finally entered the promised land.
rounds.why: Moses died on Mount Nebo in sight of the land. Joshua led Israel across the Jordan.

rounds.subject: David
truths: He pretended to be insane to escape from the king of Gath.
He was forbidden to build the temple because he was a man of war.
rounds.lie: He killed Goliath using a sword he had taken from the Philistine camp.
rounds.why: He killed Goliath with a sling and a stone, then cut off his head with Goliath's own sword.

rounds.subject: Jonah
truths: He told the sailors to throw him overboard to calm the storm.
He was angry when Nineveh repented and God spared the city.
rounds.lie: He was swallowed by a whale and stayed inside it for forty days.
rounds.why: The text says a great fish, not a whale, and the time was three days and three nights.

rounds.subject: Daniel
truths: He prayed with his windows open toward Jerusalem three times a day.
He interpreted handwriting that appeared on a palace wall during a feast.
rounds.lie: He was thrown into the fiery furnace along with his three friends.
rounds.why: Daniel was not in the furnace. He faced the lions' den; his friends faced the furnace.

rounds.subject: Solomon
truths: He asked God for wisdom instead of riches or long life.
He wrote thousands of proverbs and more than a thousand songs.
rounds.lie: He built the temple in Jerusalem in just seven weeks.
rounds.why: The temple took seven years to build, not seven weeks.

rounds.subject: Peter
truths: He cut off the ear of the high priest's servant in Gethsemane.
He was released from prison by an angel while the church prayed for him.
rounds.lie: He was the first disciple Jesus called by the Sea of Galilee.
rounds.why: Andrew followed Jesus first, then brought his brother Simon Peter to him.

rounds.subject: Paul
truths: He was a tentmaker by trade and worked to support himself.
He was shipwrecked and bitten by a viper on the island of Melita.
rounds.lie: He was one of the twelve apostles who followed Jesus during his ministry.
rounds.why: Paul never walked with Jesus during his earthly ministry. He was called after the resurrection.

rounds.subject: Samson
truths: He caught three hundred foxes and tied torches to their tails.
He killed more Philistines in his death than during his whole life.
rounds.lie: Delilah cut his hair herself while he slept on her knees.
rounds.why: She called for a man to shave off the seven locks of his head.

rounds.subject: Joseph
truths: He was sold to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver.
He named his first son Manasseh, meaning God made him forget his toil.
rounds.lie: He was thirty-nine years old when he stood before Pharaoh.
rounds.why: Joseph was thirty years old when he entered Pharaoh's service.

rounds.subject: Elijah
truths: He outran a chariot all the way to Jezreel.
He heard God not in the wind or fire, but in a still small voice.
rounds.lie: He was fed by ravens that brought him bread and water each morning.
rounds.why: The ravens brought bread and flesh. He drank water from the brook.

rounds.subject: Esther
truths: She hid her Jewish identity on her cousin's instruction.
She invited the king and Haman to two banquets before making her request.
rounds.lie: She was the first wife of King Ahasuerus.
rounds.why: Vashti was queen first, and was deposed before Esther was chosen.

rounds.subject: John the Baptist
truths: He leaped in his mother's womb when Mary greeted Elisabeth.
He sent disciples from prison to ask if Jesus was the one to come.
rounds.lie: He baptized Jesus in the Sea of Galilee.
rounds.why: He baptized Jesus in the river Jordan, not the Sea of Galilee.

rounds.subject: Abraham
truths: He twice said his wife was his sister out of fear.
He bought a cave at Machpelah as a burial place for Sarah.
rounds.lie: He was seventy-five years old when Isaac was born.
rounds.why: He was seventy-five when he left Haran. Isaac was born when he was a hundred.

rounds.subject: The plagues of Egypt
truths: The magicians reproduced the plague of frogs but could not stop it.
The plague of darkness lasted three days across all Egypt.
rounds.lie: There were seven plagues in total before Pharaoh let Israel go.
rounds.why: There were ten plagues, ending with the death of the firstborn.

rounds.subject: The ark of the covenant
truths: It held the tables of stone, Aaron's rod that budded, and a pot of manna.
A man named Uzzah died after touching it to steady it.
rounds.lie: It was carried into battle at Jericho on a new cart.
rounds.why: It was carried by priests on staves around Jericho. The new cart came much later, under the Philistines and then David.

rounds.subject: Ruth
truths: She gleaned in the field of Boaz, a near kinsman of her husband.
She became the great-grandmother of King David.
rounds.lie: She was from Midian and married into an Israelite family.
rounds.why: Ruth was a Moabite, not a Midianite.

rounds.subject: The twelve spies
truths: They brought back a cluster of grapes carried between two men on a staff.
They spent forty days searching out the land of Canaan.
rounds.lie: Only Joshua brought back a good report of the land.
rounds.why: Two men brought back a good report: Joshua and Caleb.

rounds.subject: Jacob
truths: He worked fourteen years to marry Rachel after being deceived with Leah.
He saw a ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending.
rounds.lie: He had twelve sons and no daughters.
rounds.why: He also had a daughter named Dinah.

rounds.subject: Gideon
truths: He tested God twice using a fleece and the morning dew.
He was threshing wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites.
rounds.lie: He attacked the Midianites with three thousand chosen men.
rounds.why: His army was reduced to three hundred men before the attack.

rounds.subject: The birth of Jesus
truths: Angels announced the birth to shepherds keeping watch over their flocks.
Joseph was warned in a dream to flee into Egypt.
rounds.lie: Three wise men visited the stable on the night he was born.
rounds.why: The number of wise men is never given, and they came to a house, not the stable, some time later.

rounds.subject: The feeding of the five thousand
truths: A boy's five barley loaves and two small fish were used.
Twelve baskets of fragments were gathered afterward.
rounds.lie: The five thousand counted included women and children.
rounds.why: The text says about five thousand men, beside women and children.

rounds.subject: The crucifixion
truths: Darkness covered the land from the sixth hour to the ninth hour.
The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
rounds.lie: The soldiers broke Jesus' legs to hasten his death.
rounds.why: They broke the legs of the two thieves, but found Jesus already dead and did not break his.

rounds.subject: Lazarus
truths: He had been in the grave four days before Jesus arrived.
The chief priests plotted to kill him as well, because of him many believed.
rounds.lie: He was a stranger Jesus met on the road to Bethany.
rounds.why: He was a close friend, the brother of Mary and Martha.

rounds.subject: The ten commandments
truths: They were written on both sides of two tables of stone.
Moses broke the first set at the foot of the mountain.
rounds.lie: They were given to Moses on Mount Horeb after forty days of rain.
rounds.why: They were given on Mount Sinai, and Moses was there forty days and forty nights without rain.

rounds.subject: Joshua
truths: He commanded the sun to stand still over Gibeon.
He was Moses' minister long before he led Israel.
rounds.lie: The walls of Jericho fell on the seventh day after seven trumpet blasts.
rounds.why: On the seventh day they circled the city seven times, not once with seven blasts.

rounds.subject: Saul
truths: He was from the tribe of Benjamin, the smallest tribe of Israel.
He once prophesied among the prophets, to everyone's surprise.
rounds.lie: He was killed by David in the final battle against the Philistines.
rounds.why: Saul fell on his own sword at Gilboa. David was not in that battle.

rounds.subject: The tower of Babel
truths: The builders used brick for stone and slime for mortar.
The Lord confounded their language so they could not understand each other.
rounds.lie: God destroyed the tower with fire from heaven.
rounds.why: God scattered the people and confused their speech. The tower was simply left unfinished.

rounds.subject: Job
truths: His three friends sat with him seven days without speaking a word.
He was given twice as much as he had before at the end.
rounds.lie: God explained to Job exactly why he had suffered.
rounds.why: God never explained the reason. He answered Job out of the whirlwind with questions instead.

rounds.subject: Mary and Martha
truths: Martha was cumbered about much serving while Mary sat at Jesus' feet.
Martha confessed that Jesus was the Christ, the Son of God.
rounds.lie: Jesus rebuked Mary for neglecting her duties in the house.
rounds.why: He defended Mary, saying she had chosen the good part that would not be taken from her.

rounds.subject: The day of Pentecost
truths: There came a sound from heaven like a rushing mighty wind.
About three thousand souls were added that day.
rounds.lie: The disciples spoke in a language no one present could understand.
rounds.why: Every man heard them speak in his own language, which is why the crowd was amazed.

rounds.subject: Zacchaeus
truths: He climbed a sycamore tree because he was short of stature.
He promised to give half his goods to the poor.
rounds.lie: He was a fisherman in Jericho who left his nets to follow Jesus.
rounds.why: He was a chief tax collector, and a rich one.

rounds.subject: Cain and Abel
truths: Abel brought the firstlings of his flock and their fat.
Cain was marked by God so that no one finding him would kill him.
rounds.lie: Cain was struck dead immediately after killing his brother.
rounds.why: Cain lived on, became a fugitive, and built a city named after his son Enoch.

rounds.subject: The walls of Jerusalem
truths: Nehemiah inspected the ruined walls by night before telling anyone his plan.
The builders worked with a weapon in one hand and a tool in the other.
rounds.lie: The wall was finished in fifty-two weeks.
rounds.why: The wall was finished in fifty-two days.

rounds.subject: Balaam
truths: His donkey saw the angel of the Lord before he did.
He was hired by Balak to curse Israel but blessed them instead.
rounds.lie: He struck his donkey twice before it finally spoke to him.
rounds.why: He struck it three times, and the donkey asked why he had smitten it these three times.

rounds.subject: Hezekiah
truths: He spread a threatening letter before the Lord in the house of the Lord.
He was granted fifteen more years of life after weeping before God.
rounds.lie: The sign God gave him was the sun standing still at noon.
rounds.why: The sign was the shadow on the sundial going backward ten degrees.

rounds.subject: The prodigal son
truths: He was sent into the fields to feed swine.
His father saw him while he was still a great way off and ran to him.
rounds.lie: His older brother welcomed him home with the rest of the household.
rounds.why: The elder brother was angry and refused to go in.

rounds.subject: Stephen
truths: His face appeared as the face of an angel to the council.
Saul of Tarsus consented to his death and kept the witnesses' clothes.
rounds.lie: He was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.
rounds.why: He was one of the seven chosen to serve tables, not one of the twelve.

rounds.subject: The Red Sea crossing
truths: A strong east wind blew all night and made the sea dry land.
A pillar of cloud came between Israel and the Egyptians.
rounds.lie: Moses struck the water with his hand to divide it.
rounds.why: He stretched out his hand with the rod over the sea.

rounds.subject: Rahab
truths: She hid the spies under stalks of flax on her roof.
She and all her father's household were spared when Jericho fell.
rounds.lie: She hung a white cloth from her window as the agreed sign.
rounds.why: The sign was a line of scarlet thread.
